title: G 55 AMG
verdict: AMG gave a 1970s military truck up to 507 PS (500 hp) and changed almost nothing else. It's fast in a straight line, still has three lockers, and drinks fuel at a rate that makes a G 500 look economical.

paragraphs: The G 55 AMG is the G that made speed part of the G-Wagen's reputation. AMG took the ladder-framed, solid-axle [[g-class/w463|W463]], fitted its own 5.4-litre V8 and later a supercharger, and sold it through the regular showroom from 1999 into 2012. It still has full-time four-wheel drive, low range and three locking differentials. It also has 700 Nm of torque and a top speed limited to 210 km/h, which is about as fast as anyone should drive something with this shape.

story.heading: AMG'S SECOND TRY
paragraphs: AMG had tuned a G before. In 1993, 13 of the 446 [[g-class/500ge|500 GEs]] got AMG's 6.0-litre upgrade kit. The G 55 was different because anyone could order one. Introduced in 1999, it was the most powerful G yet: 354 PS (349 hp) and 525 Nm from AMG's naturally aspirated M113 V8, with 0–100 km/h in 7.4 seconds. That made it about four seconds quicker than the 500 GE to 100 km/h.

When Mercedes-Benz USA took over G distribution from [[g-class/europa|Europa International]] for the 2002 model year, the G 55 AMG launched alongside the [[g-class/g500|G 500]] as the only other G-Class in American showrooms. Hagerty credits the AMG with pushing US G sales higher in the following years.

story.heading: THE KOMPRESSOR YEARS
paragraphs: In 2004 (the 2005 model year in the US) AMG added a supercharger. The M113K, the same supercharged 5.4 used in the era's CL 55 and SL 55, made 476 PS (469 hp) and 700 Nm, cutting 0–100 km/h to about 5.6 seconds. From 2006 it was rated at 500 PS. For 2009 a new engine control unit raised it to 507 PS (500 hp), with torque unchanged.

The 2009 update also brought a three-bar grille, Kompressor lettering, polished 19-inch AMG wheels on 275/55 R19 tyres, an anthracite Alcantara headliner, designo leather, COMAND APS and a stronger ESP with hill-start assist. All G 55s used the five-speed 722.6 automatic. Some enthusiasts prefer that well-proven gearbox to the seven-speed fitted to later Gs.

story.heading: HOW IT ENDED
paragraphs: The G 55's last US model year was 2011. For 2012 the US G-Class range was just the [[g-class/g550|G 550]]. In 2012 AMG replaced the supercharged 5.4 with a 5.5-litre biturbo V8 and renamed the truck G 63 AMG, arriving in the US for 2013. That made the G 55 the last AMG G with a supercharger and the five-speed automatic.

Values have settled well above ordinary G 500s. autoevolution's study of 2019–2022 auctions found average Kompressor prices around $60,000 in 2021–22, with low-mileage 2011 trucks reaching $72,500 and $94,000. High-mileage 2005 and 2007 trucks sold for $27,000–40,000. For an off-roader, those cheaper, well-serviced trucks are the interesting ones. You don't need perfect paint to use the lockers.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · NATURALLY ASPIRATED OR KOMPRESSOR?
callout.title: Two very different G 55s
paragraphs: The early G 55 (2002–2004 model years in the US) uses AMG's naturally aspirated M113 5.4: 349 hp, about 400 lb-ft, 0–100 km/h in 7.4 seconds. The Kompressor (US 2005–2011) has a supercharger and an intercooler, with 469–500 hp and 516 lb-ft, and gets there in about 5.5 seconds.

For trail use the trade-off is simple. The naturally aspirated truck has fewer parts to fail: no supercharger, no intercooler pump, and less heat under the hood. The Kompressor is quicker and newer and has the later interior updates, but it needs its supplemental cooling system kept in good order. German Cars For Sale Blog found the naturally aspirated trucks commanding a big premium over a contemporary G 500 for low-mileage examples.

engineering_intro: Beneath the side pipes, the G 55 is still a W463. The body sits on a separate ladder frame. Both axles are solid and coil-sprung. A two-speed transfer case drives all four wheels all the time, and there are three lockers on the dash. AMG changed the engine, the brakes, the wheels and arches, and the cabin. The driveline layout that wins off-road stayed the same.

engineering.note: Long-wheelbase five-door for the US; AMG wide fenders and stainless running boards.
Coil-sprung and link-located; independent front suspension didn't arrive until 2018.
Three 100% locks plus low range, as on every W463.
Supercharged and intercooled, 476→507 PS, 700 Nm. US 2005–2011.
Used for the G 55's whole production run.

engineering_note.title: KEEP THE KOMPRESSOR COOL
engineering_note.body: The supercharged engine cools its intake charge through an intercooler fed by an electric circulation pump. When the pump fails the engine heat-soaks and loses power, which hurts most at low speed in hot weather — exactly how a G gets driven off-road. Treat the intercooler pump as a wear item.

generations_table.note: Supercharged; US from MY2005; 0–100 km/h ≈ 5.6 s
Power bump; OE tires 285/55R18 in the US
New ECU, three-bar grille, 19-inch wheels, COMAND APS; last US MY2011

buying_checks.head: Is it really an AMG?
buying_checks.body: Plenty of G 500s and G 550s have been dressed as AMGs. Check the VIN and the data card, not the badges.

buying_checks.head: Naturally aspirated or supercharged?
buying_checks.body: US 2002–2004 trucks are naturally aspirated; 2005–2011 are Kompressors. Make sure the model year, VIN and engine all match the price.

buying_checks.head: Heat soak and the intercooler pump
buying_checks.body: On a Kompressor, ask when the intercooler pump was replaced. A truck that pulls hard when cold and goes flat when hot is the classic symptom.

buying_checks.head: Listen at idle
buying_checks.body: Vibration or an RPM-dependent chirp on the M113 points to the harmonic balancer. Don't drive far on a failing one.

buying_checks.head: Mounts and suspension
buying_checks.body: Commenters on German Cars For Sale Blog advise checking engine and transmission mounts and suspension wear. With 700 Nm going through them, mounts wear out faster.

buying_checks.head: Test all three lockers
buying_checks.body: Engage the centre, rear and front locks on loose ground. Lockers that 'were never used' by the last owner often don't work.

buying_checks.head: Rust, even on the fancy one
buying_checks.body: Owners warn G 55s rust like any G, especially near the coast. Check the tailgate's lower edge, door bottoms, sills and rear frame tubes.

buying_checks.head: Gear oil behind the front wheels
buying_checks.body: Oil on the inner wheels or the large AMG calipers means front axle seals, and possibly contaminated brakes.

repairs.title: Intercooler pump (Kompressor)
repairs.symptoms: Power drops after heat soak, especially in traffic or at crawling speed; intake temperatures climb.
repairs.fix: Replace the electric intercooler circulation pump with the updated Bosch unit, then bleed the low-temperature circuit. Victory Road Performance recommends replacing it as routine maintenance because the original pump failed often. GwagenParts sells a higher-flow bolt-in pump for 2006–2010 G 55s.
repairs.tools: Updated Bosch intercooler pump or upgrade pump · coolant · hose clamps · bleeding funnel

parts.name: Bosch intercooler pump kit with coolant (G 55 2005–11)

repairs.title: Harmonic balancer (M113)
repairs.symptoms: Vibration at idle, a wobbling crank pulley, cracked or bulging rubber, chirp or rattle that changes with RPM. If the outer ring lets go you lose the belt drive.
repairs.fix: Remove the belt, lock the crank with a counter-hold tool, and replace the balancer with a new torque-to-yield centre bolt and a new front crank seal.
repairs.tools: Crank counter-hold tool · 27 mm socket · breaker bar or high-torque impact · new balancer, centre bolt and crank seal

refs.name: G500 / G55 serpentine belt routing diagram (ClubGWagen forum)

repairs.title: Engine & transmission mounts
repairs.symptoms: Clunk on take-off or shifts, extra vibration in the cabin, engine movement when you blip the throttle.
repairs.fix: Replace the fluid-filled engine mounts (VRP notes they leak and collapse, and wear quickly in high-power cars) and the transmission mount together. Support the engine from below and lift each side in turn.
repairs.tools: Engine support or jack with wood block · sockets and extensions · new engine and transmission mounts

repairs.title: Spark plugs, wires & coils
repairs.symptoms: Misfire codes, rough idle, hesitation under boost. Many owners don't know when the plugs were last done.
repairs.fix: Replace all 16 plugs (the M113 has twin plugs per cylinder) and inspect the wires and coil packs. VRP suggests heavier-insulated wires if the originals are tired. Fix any misfire before adding power.
repairs.tools: Spark plug socket and extensions · dielectric grease · plugs · wires · coils if needed

parts.name: NGK ILFR6A spark plug (G 55 Kompressor, need 16)
Bosch FR8DPP33 spark plugs, set of 16

repairs.title: 722.6 service & 13-pin connector
repairs.symptoms: Harsh or delayed shifts, limp mode, or ATF wicking into the wiring at the gearbox connector.
repairs.fix: Drop the pan, replace the filter and fluid, and check the 13-pin connector (203-540-02-53) for leaks. VRP says to check the conductor plate too in many cases. Use the correct Mercedes-spec ATF and fill by temperature.
repairs.tools: ATF · filter and pan gasket · 13-pin connector (203-540-02-53) · dipstick tool

parts.name: FUCHS 722.6 ATF service kit (fluid, filter, gasket)

repairs.title: Diff locks won't engage
repairs.symptoms: One or all locks refuse to engage or drop out. On mid-2000s W463s the centre lock is vacuum-operated and the axle locks hydraulic, so one vacuum leak can disable the whole sequence.
repairs.fix: Confirm vacuum at the transfer-case hose, then work back through the pump, reservoir and switchover valve block with a tee-in gauge. One 2005 owner's fault was a split plastic connector inside a rubber Y-fitting under the brake booster. Bleed the hydraulic lines and change the fluids while you're there.
repairs.tools: Hand vacuum pump with gauge · vacuum tees and line · connectors · diff and transfer-case fluid · bleeding kit

repairs.title: Front axle seal leak
repairs.symptoms: Gear oil on the inner front wheels, a gear-oil smell, oil on the caliper or rotor, brakes pulling.
repairs.fix: Replace both front axle seals and inspect the shafts. Replace contaminated pads and resurface or replace the rotors. Oil on brakes this big is not something to leave.
repairs.tools: Axle seals (both sides) · seal driver · gear oil · pads and rotors if contaminated

parts.name: Genuine Mercedes front axle shaft seal 009 997 28 47
Red Line 75W-90 GL-5 gear oil (1 qt)

repairs.title: Steering damper & front-end wander
repairs.symptoms: Wander and wheel shake at 55–70 mph, vague on-centre feel, front-end clunks. On a 500 hp truck you'll notice it quickly.
repairs.fix: Swap the steering damper (OEM or an upgrade such as a Bilstein B6), check the drag link and tie-rod ends, then align.
repairs.tools: Steering damper · sockets and wrenches · tie-rod/drag-link ends if worn

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: About 33 inches on 18-inch wheels. Owners of unlifted W463s on Expedition Portal run 275/70R18 with no rubbing on sensible offsets, and 285/65R18 with a slight rub at full left lock. Fitment data lists 285/55R18 for 2004 and 2008 US G 55s, so 18s clear those brakes. One owner warns 18s won't clear G 63 brakes, so test-fit before buying 18s for a 19-inch 2009–2011 truck. Re-code the tire size so the speedometer and ESP stay accurate.

faq.q: What size are the factory tires?
faq.a: 285/55R18 on US trucks through 2008 (Goodyear and TireSize.com fitment data). The 2009 update moved to 275/55R19 on 9.5-inch-wide AMG wheels.
In the US, 2002–2004 G 55s are naturally aspirated (349 hp) and 2005–2011 are Kompressors (469 hp, later 493 and 500 hp). In Europe the supercharger arrived in 2004.

faq.q: Does it have low range and lockers?
faq.a: Yes. It's a full W463 with permanent four-wheel drive, a two-speed transfer case and centre, rear and front locking differentials. AMG didn't take any of that out.
7,000 lb with a braked trailer, according to the spec data on a 2005 example. Check your owner's manual and trailer brakes.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: EPA figures are 12 mpg city, 14 highway and 13 combined for the 2003 naturally aspirated truck, and 11 city, 13 highway and 12 combined for Kompressors such as the 2005 and 2011. Bigger tires and a rack will make it worse.

An MBWorld owner who drove both found the gap smaller than expected: the G 550's 382 hp feels quick, but the G 55 has power in reserve at any speed, feels tighter and is much louder. For trail use they're mechanically the same truck; the G 55 adds supercharger cooling to maintain.
The last US model year was 2011. The 2012 US range was only the G 550, and the 5.5-litre biturbo G 63 AMG replaced the G 55 in 2012 (the 2013 model year in the US).

The frame, axles and V8 are strong. Common jobs are predictable: the intercooler pump on Kompressors, the harmonic balancer, mounts, front axle seals, the steering damper and locker vacuum lines. One owner commenting on German Cars For Sale Blog calls the windshield a consumable. Buy on service records, not low mileage. On 2002–04 trucks, also test every window, lock and seat. Handsome Motors says those early electrical gremlins were mostly gone by 2005–06.

autoevolution's 2019–2022 auction study found Kompressor averages around $60,000 in 2021–22, with high-mileage 2005–2007 trucks at $27,000–40,000 and low-mileage 2011s up to $94,000. Deep Black and Fire Opal Red cars sold best.

mods.why: On a Kompressor, cooling is the first upgrade: a higher-flow intercooler pump and optionally a split cooling circuit so the supercharger's loop isn't heated by the engine's.
A modest spring lift and better dampers improve clearance and control the weight of a heavy V8 truck off-road.
G-specific builders can add armour, racks and lighting without making the AMG look like a costume.
Flat platform racks and rear ladders for tents and recovery gear.
Brabus-style kits that bring 4×4²-inspired stance and capability to a standard W463.
Swap the 19s for 18s (where the brakes allow) and fit taller all-terrains. It's the biggest improvement off-road.

baseline_service.intro: Baseline everything the week you buy it. The G 55 adds an AMG engine, and from 2005 a supercharger with its own low-temperature intercooler circuit, to a W463 chassis that still needs knuckle, axle and diff-lock care. Note which engine you have: 2003–04 US trucks are naturally aspirated, 2005-on are Kompressor (M113K), and several parts differ.

items.interval: Then yearly or at the service indicator
items.note: Same top-mounted cartridge filter as the M113 G 500. If an oil cooler is drained you'll need extra oil.

items.note: A dirty filter costs a supercharged engine more than an NA one — don't stretch it.
